solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Launder diamonds, the proceeds of larceny

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: what proceeds from a word is something made out of it, so its letters are reworked here

explanation.surface: A villain cleans up stolen gems, the loot from a theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launder' suggests money-laundering, which fits the larceny theme, but it is simply the cleaning definition. 'proceeds of' rearranges LARCENY into RYCLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to clean clothes, the hyphenated one using solvents rather than water.

clue.text: Capital "O" that signifies "R"

definitions.note: in the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter R is spoken with this code word

parts.note: Rome is the capital city of Italy

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about a capital letter O that somehow stands for R.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like it qualifies the letter O as upper case, but it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio phonetic alphabet assigns a code word to each letter; this is the code word for R.

clue.text: G8's leisure facility?

parts.note: the G8 is a club of eight leading nations, so its clubhouse would whimsically be a club for countries

explanation.walkthrough: The G8 was a forum of eight major economies; read literally, a club whose members are countries.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural sports and social club with golf and tennis, here reimagined as a club of nations.

clue.text: They vote in line in Chicago City hills

parts.note: the El is Chicago's elevated railway line
EC is the postcode area of the City of London
tors are rocky hills on Dartmoor and similar uplands

explanation.surface: Chicago residents queue to cast ballots in the city's hilly districts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' is London's financial district, whose postcode begins EC; tors are rocky hilltops in southwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: Those entitled to cast ballots in an election are its voters, collectively the electorate.

clue.text: Rank speculative scripts, all rejected except the fourth?

indicators.note: leave out the fourth letter of the phrase just built, which drops the E of none

parts.note: scripts sent in on spec that were all turned down: none commissioned

explanation.surface: A writer grumbles that all their unsolicited scripts were turned down bar one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except the fourth' sounds like the fourth script was accepted; it actually removes the fourth letter, E, from NONE COMMISSIONED.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergeants and corporals hold ranks without an officer's commission, describing that tier of the military.

clue.text: It cuts errors in demonstrations

indicators.note: the word it cuts into the other piece, splitting it open

parts.note: sins are moral errors or wrongdoings

explanation.surface: Something trims the mistakes found in product demonstrations.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters occupying a building in protest stage these as demonstrations.

clue.text: It's modified, genetically modified, on a flower part

indicators.note: changed in form, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of it's, without the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A botanist explains that some flower has been altered by genetic engineering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' does two jobs: alone it is the anagram signal, and within 'genetically modified' it is part of a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically, this is the pollen-receiving tip of a flower's pistil.

clue.text: Ends of plant, the camellia

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the three following words is taken

explanation.surface: A gardener points to the tips of a camellia bush.
explanation.walkthrough: The tea plant is Camellia sinensis, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaves brewed for the drink come from a camellia species, so the plant is literally that shrub.

clue.text: Month with ace racing non-stop all over country

indicators.note: the whole assembled string is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August
A is the playing-card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: without its stop, i.e. its last letter cut off

explanation.surface: A month of ace motor racing without a break all over the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-stop' trims racing to RACIN; AUG + A + RACIN is AUGARACIN, which 'all over' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American republic between Honduras and Costa Rica, so an example of a nation.

clue.text: Wall in green at shed

indicators.note: cast off, so these two letters are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: green means inexperienced or unripe, i.e. immature

explanation.surface: Brick in a building painted green beside a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' and 'shed' look like a garden scene; green is inexperienced, and shed is a verb losing AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclose someone within walls, imprisoning them, is a literary verb for walling in.

clue.text: Sister these days is a boring pest

indicators.note: drilling into, so these words go inside the other piece

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
taken as written
taken as written
CE, Common Era, marks the current era of dates

explanation.surface: A nurse complains that the ward sister is tiresome lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' sounds like the sister is dull, but it means drilling into. 'these days' is the Common Era abbreviation used in dates.
explanation.definitionFit: An annoying person or thing is a pest or bother.

clue.text: Kick start

definitions.meaning: to strike with the foot, as with footwear

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to kick something and to start a computer, from bootstrap.

clue.text: Engineers smoke a lot at work, stifling resistance

indicators.note: smothering, so the rearranged letters enclose the other piece
working on the letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Factory engineers who puff away on the job, smothering any objection.
explanation.walkthrough: The smoking picture hides the mechanics: 'at work' shuffles the three words and 'stifling' wraps the result round the resistance symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftsmen who make tools and dies are precision engineers in a workshop.

clue.text: He'll like raw flounders

indicators.note: struggles clumsily, so the letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: the letters of he'll without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A predator will enjoy uncooked flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flounders' looks like the fish on the menu, but it is the anagram signal; the whole clue also describes the orca's diet.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca, a large black-and-white toothed predator, eats fish raw, so the clue describes it.

clue.text: Label girl cut off, upset about front of gown

indicators.note: around, so the overturned string surrounds the letter that follows
overturned, so the girl and the cutting word together are read backwards

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
to lop is to cut off

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A girl's dress label snipped off and turned over around the neckline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MARYLOP into POLYRAM, which then goes 'about' G. 'Label' is a record company, not a tag in a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known record company, and a record company is a label in the music business.

clue.text: Use subcontractors to build courthouse, not hospital

indicators.note: building from the letters means rearranging them into something new

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A council hires contractors to construct a courthouse instead of a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hospital' removes H from COURTHOUSE before 'to build' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Contracting work out to an outside supplier is to hand it to subcontractors.

clue.text: A sign ladies have drunk gallons

indicators.note: having taken in, so the toilet holds the letter

parts.note: the ladies is a toilet, a loo

explanation.surface: A telltale sign that women have been knocking back drink by the gallon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladies' is the toilet, informally a loo in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's emblem is a graphic sign identifying it.

clue.text: Some say you'll change over Christmas

indicators.note: said aloud by some speakers, so a word that sounds like it

parts.note: you'll is pronounced the same as the old word for the festive season
a tide is a turning or change, as in the tide turning

explanation.surface: People insist you'll alter your ways over Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The festive season around December 25th has an old name meaning the Yule season.

clue.text: Scrap odd bits of meatballs etc

indicators.note: throw away the first, third and fifth letters and so on, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Throw out the odd lumps of meatballs and similar leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a scrap of food; it says to discard the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both Latin abbreviations stand for 'and the rest' or 'and others' at the end of a list.

clue.text: In which to cook small golden pecan nuts

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A recipe step: cook small golden pecan nuts in this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like part of 'pecan nuts' but rearranges PECAN into CEPAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-handled pot is a vessel used for cooking on the hob.

clue.text: Old city has a role in it

indicators.note: the role sits inside the other piece

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA
a part is an actor's role

explanation.surface: An ancient city plays its part in some story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the sense of sex appeal is SA, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek city-state of antiquity famed for its warriors.

clue.text: By spinning one in alcohol win derisory award

indicators.note: the three pieces sit inside the drink

parts.note: booze is slang for alcohol
PR, public relations, is the business of spin
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A drunk wins a mocking prize by spinning one into his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' looks like a reversal signal, but it is PR, public relations spin.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke prize given to the person who finishes last is a mocking award.

clue.text: Trounce London team initially, putting on pressure

indicators.note: adding something after, so the next letter is placed on the end

parts.note: West Ham United, a London football club, by its initials
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A London football side starts by pressing hard to thrash opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham United is a London football club; its initials give WHU.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal American verb meaning to beat decisively, to thrash or defeat soundly.

clue.text: Employ Ford parts making up Russian order

indicators.note: splits open, so the car goes between the letters

parts.note: to employ is to use
the Ka is a small Ford car

explanation.surface: Ford components assemble a Russian request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like car components, but it is a verb: the Ka splits USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar's edict in imperial Russia, hence any arbitrary decree or command.

clue.text: Golf club straddles free football field

indicators.note: sits either side of, so these letters wrap around the middle piece

parts.note: G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an iron is a type of golf club
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A golf club straddling a free football pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The gridded playing area in American football is its field.

clue.text: Racket regularly used by Agassi at Wimbledon finals

indicators.note: every other one of those final letters
the final letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A tennis racket Agassi regularly used in the Wimbledon finals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finals' takes the last letters D, Y, I, T, N; 'regularly' keeps every other one.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud noise or din is a racket, a sense far from the tennis bat.

clue.text: Book One has returned with "Excellent" inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: goes within the reversed word
turned back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A book someone has brought back with a glowing review tucked inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' sounds like a library book but reverses HAS to SAH; AI is A1.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophetic book of the Old Testament, so one of the Bible's books.

clue.text: Woman's involved in a medical breakthrough

parts.note: her refers to a woman

indicators.note: twisted together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman plays a part in a major medical advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakthrough' looks like a discovery but means an organ breaking through the muscle wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A rupture where an organ pushes through the abdominal wall is literally a breakthrough of tissue.

clue.text: Dredged place divers prefer bordering mouth of Exe

indicators.note: lying on both sides of, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: divers jump in at the deep end of a pool

indicators.note: the first letter, the opening of the word; Exe is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: A river mouth was dredged to make a spot divers like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouth of Exe' suggests an estuary, but it is the letter E. The Exe is a river in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dredging a channel removes silt and makes it lower, so the waterway was made lower.
